innate.name: Private research that goes deeper than the room
innate.behavior: You will take a question that others answer with a quick search and spend an evening, then a week, then a month on it — reading primary sources, testing small cases, keeping notes nobody asked for. When a colleague asks how you know something obscure, you can trace the path back through three sources you checked yourself. You do not wait for a course or a manager to assign the learning; you open the file and start. The output is not a report but a working model in your head that you can apply the next time the same problem appears.
innate.evidence: Indirect Resource is the single heaviest god in the chart, appearing on the month stem and repeating in the hidden stems of the month, day, and hour branches. The Day Master is balanced, with metal and earth named as the favorable elements, so this research energy feeds the core rather than draining it.

innate.name: Converting findings into steady, incremental income
innate.behavior: You do not chase a single large payout. You take what you have learned and turn it into a small, repeatable service — a template, a checklist, a short engagement, a fix you can sell again. You price it modestly, deliver it reliably, and then improve the same offer rather than inventing a new one. Over a year the sum of these small conversions is visible, but at any single moment it looks unremarkable. You keep a mental ledger of which findings actually paid and which only interested you.
innate.evidence: Direct Wealth is tied with Rob Wealth as the second-heaviest force, showing on the year stem and in hidden stems of the year and day branches. The Day Master is balanced, so the wealth step is not a stretch — it is the natural middle of the loop from research to income.

innate.name: Defending ground you have opened against peers
innate.behavior: When someone else starts offering what you built, you do not panic and you do not escalate loudly. You go back to the source, add a layer they have not copied, and make your version harder to replace. In a meeting you will quietly correct a competitor's claim with a detail only you have checked. You treat competition as a signal that the ground is worth holding, not as a reason to abandon it. The defense is usually technical, not personal.
innate.evidence: Rob Wealth is tied with Direct Wealth at the second-heaviest weight, sitting on the hour stem and in a hidden stem of the year branch. The loop runs from Indirect Resource into Rob Wealth, so peer competition is a structural step, not an accident.

trained.name: Producing visible output on a deadline
trained.behavior: You have learned to package research into something another person can use by a fixed date — a summary, a handover, a short deliverable. Left alone you would keep refining, but you now set an external date and ship even when the work feels unfinished. In practice this looks like sending the draft on Friday rather than the following Tuesday, or writing the one-page version when you would rather write the ten-page one. It is a real skill, but it does not come from the chart's lead force.
trained.trained_by: The chart's lead force is private research, and the loop returns to research after peer competition. Nothing in the structure pushes finished output outward on its own, so the habit of shipping was built by an environment that required visible results — school, employers, or clients who would not accept 'still working on it' as an answer.
trained.evidence: Eating God carries no weight at all, and Direct Officer also carries no weight, so neither natural output nor formal position supplies the push to finish and present. The current luck pillar starting at age 38 is Ren Wu, and the chart notes that the pull toward private study loosens in the decade beginning around age 48 with the Gui Wei pillar — meaning the shipping habit is being learned against the grain of the structure, not from it.

defensive.name: Competing for the same resources as peers
defensive.looks_like: Outsiders see someone who is good at holding territory — you notice when a colleague is angling for the same budget, the same client, or the same credit, and you move to protect your position. It reads as sharp political awareness or healthy competitiveness.
defensive.actual_cost: It drains you because the chart's center of gravity is private study, not peer contest. Each round of defending ground pulls you away from the research that actually feeds you, and the loop then sends you back to study to recover — so you spend energy on the defense and then more energy rebuilding the depth you lost. The visible result is slow accumulation and a feeling of never getting to point at something finished.
defensive.evidence: Rob Wealth is tied with Direct Wealth at the second-heaviest weight and sits on the hour stem, closing the loop after the income step. The chart's own core loop describes peers noticing the ground you opened and competing for the same resources, which pushes you back into private study — a cycle that costs energy rather than restoring it.

defensive.name: Waiting for formal standing before acting
defensive.looks_like: You can appear to be someone who respects hierarchy — you wait for the title, the approval, or the official role before you push a piece of work forward. To others this looks like professionalism or patience.
defensive.actual_cost: It is a compensatory pause, not a strength. The chart gives formal position no weight, so waiting for it means waiting for something the structure does not supply. The cost is that research sits on your desk longer than it needs to, and the incremental income step is delayed while you look for permission that is not coming from the chart's own logic.
defensive.evidence: Direct Officer carries no weight at all — no stem or hidden stem in the chart classifies under it. The lead force is Indirect Resource, which operates outside formal hierarchy, and the secondary forces are Direct Wealth and Rob Wealth, neither of which is a position of authority.

one_leverage: Keep the private research ability. It is the heaviest single force in the chart, it appears on the month stem and repeats in three hidden branches, and the Day Master is balanced with metal and earth as favorable elements — so using it returns energy rather than spending it. The other two innate abilities depend on it: the incremental income step only works because the research produces something worth selling, and the defense against peers only works because you have ground worth defending. If you had to drop everything else, the research is the one that keeps regenerating the loop. The trained shipping habit and the defensive competition are useful, but they cost energy; the research is the only ability that pays you back while you use it.
